title: SOLID Principles

sections.markdown: SOLID is five OO design principles that reduce coupling and increase cohesion, making code easier to extend, test and maintain.

rows: Open to extend, closed to modify

sections.markdown: **SRP violation**: a God class that validates input, hits the DB, sends emails AND formats reports. Any change risks breaking unrelated features.
**LSP violation**: Square extends Rectangle, but setting width also changes height, breaking code that expected a Rectangle. If a subtype surprises callers, model it differently.
SOLID is the foundation of Clean Architecture. DIP + injection is what lets you unit-test business logic with fakes instead of a real database.

flashcards.back: Single Responsibility — a class should have one reason to change.
Open for extension, closed for modification — add behavior by adding code, not editing existing code.
Depending on an injected abstraction lets you substitute a fake implementation in unit tests.

quiz.q: A class with one reason to change follows…
quiz.explain: SRP says each class should have a single responsibility / reason to change.
Liskov Substitution requires subtypes to behave as their base type.

quiz.q: Depending on abstractions, not concretions, is…
quiz.explain: Dependency Inversion Principle — depend on interfaces, inject implementations.

challenges.text: Refactor a God class into single-responsibility classes.
Add a feature by extension only (prove OCP).
Introduce a repository interface + DI so business logic is testable with a fake.
Redesign an LSP-violating hierarchy and write tests passing for every subtype.
